clue.text: A military leader in charge — efficient and friendly

indicators.note: the leader of the word military is its opening letter

parts.note: efficient means capable, able

explanation.surface: A commanding officer who is both competent and pleasant to serve under.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are cordial and free of hostility.

clue.text: Superior seaman with a female following

indicators.note: the female's name comes after the seaman, following him in the answer

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor
Bess is a woman's name, standing for any female

explanation.surface: A senior sailor walks along with a woman trailing behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey of nuns is a Mother Superior, so a superior here is that convent head.

clue.text: Foreigner demanding service shown up in hotel

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the hotel word, placed in it

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid is help or service

explanation.surface: A demanding visitor from abroad is exposed at the hotel where he stays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding' is padding for the surface; the wordplay is AID turned upward to DIA, placed inside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of India is a foreigner to a British solver.

clue.text: Flying without direction, get cover of sorts

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the flying word goes around the direction

parts.note: a-wing means on the wing, in flight
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An aircraft lost without a bearing ends up under some sort of shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas shelter stretched over a shop window or deck.

clue.text: A building in which strong beams are essential

definitions.text: A building in which strong beams are essential

parts.words: A building in which strong beams are essential
parts.note: beams reads as structural timbers, but means powerful shafts of light shone out to warn ships

explanation.surface: A structural note on a building that relies on sturdy timbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower sends out bright rotating rays to guide shipping, so powerful light beams are its whole purpose.

clue.text: Demonstration of affection scares models

indicators.note: models as a verb means shapes, so the letters of scares are reshaped

explanation.surface: A loving gesture frightens off fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle stroke or touch is a show of fondness.

clue.text: Seen before run as a very fast mover

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal
lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: Someone spotted ahead of a running race, quick as anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The African gazelle-like animal is among the fastest runners on land.

clue.text: No longer wanting quiet constitutional, to be blunt

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
P, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
licit means lawful, permitted under the constitution

explanation.surface: Someone who gives up their quiet daily walk and speaks plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitutional' suggests a walk; here it means lawful, LICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit speech is direct and outspoken, leaving nothing implied.

clue.text: Rank stuff set before a worker

indicators.note: the fabric is placed in front of the worker in the answer

parts.note: stuff is cloth, and serge is a twilled woollen fabric
the ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Smelly material placed in front of a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as smelly, but it is the definition, a military grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned army grade above corporal.

clue.text: Teasing must be abandoned in time

parts.note: abandoned in the sense of wicked or dissolute, bad
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Mocking someone is something to be given up eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful banter, light humorous ribbing.

clue.text: Way up in front of the alternative, due to a lack of response

indicators.note: the way and up come first, in front of the alternative

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A road climbing ahead of another route that nobody answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state in which a person barely reacts to anything.

clue.text: Bungling agents receiving little thanks get really foul

indicators.note: the jumbled agents take the thanks inside, receiving it
bungling means botching, so the letters of agents are muddled

parts.note: TA is short informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Clumsy secret agents taking a small thank-you only make matters worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bungling' scrambles AGENTS to SGANE, which goes around TA to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Still water that stagnates turns stale and putrid.

clue.text: Sound situation for some at sea

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for situation is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a place is a position or situation

explanation.surface: A sound position for a few people out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: The flatfish lives in the sea, one of the creatures found there.

clue.text: Fabulous aircraft!

parts.note: fabulous means belonging to fable and fairy tale: the flying craft of a witch

explanation.surface: An excited cry about a wonderful plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches in folklore fly about on a besom, a twig sweeper with a handle.

clue.text: Company rights raised — it turned on malpractice

parts.note: R is right, so two of them make rights
raised means up

indicators.note: the little word it is turned around, read backwards

explanation.surface: A firm's entitlements boosted, and then it switched to dishonest dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bribery and dishonest dealing are forms of wrongdoing in office.

clue.text: Refusing disdainfully to supply information about cereals

indicators.note: the informing word goes around the cereals, about them

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
corn is grain, the cereal crops

explanation.surface: Turning down with contempt a request to report on grain crops.
explanation.walkthrough: SING is criminal slang for grassing, telling the police what you know.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating something with contempt while rejecting it.

clue.text: Doing nothing at all can be a tonic in uncertainty

indicators.note: in uncertainty means in a confused state, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Idleness might be a restorative when you are unsure what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is part of the fodder A TONIC IN, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a complete absence of activity, idleness.

clue.text: Lines about individual Italian painter

indicators.note: the lines go around the individual, about it

parts.note: lines of poetry are verse
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: Lines of poetry about a single Italian artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian Renaissance artist.

clue.text: Study form for a change

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a version is a form or variant of something

explanation.surface: A study form to fill in for an alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversion is a transformation from one state to another.

clue.text: Invented Edam?

parts.note: the word made written upward, as in a down entry, reads as the cheese name

explanation.surface: A cheese someone dreamt up.
explanation.walkthrough: Write MADE going up a down light and you read EDAM, the Dutch cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up story is fabricated, invented.

clue.text: Spirit imbibed by the tipsy cheerfully enough

indicators.note: the answer is drunk down, contained within the words the tipsy cheerfully

explanation.surface: Liquor happily drunk by the merry tippler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' tempts as a drink; it is the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind.

clue.text: A French subordinate's ultimatum?

parts.note: un is French for a
less means lower, of lesser rank, and the 's is is

explanation.surface: A junior French official issues a final demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: an ultimatum is typically 'do this, unless...'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a condition with a threat, and the conjunction introduces that condition.

clue.text: A builder losing his head when the minister appears

indicators.note: the builder word drops its opening letter, its head

parts.note: an erector is someone who builds or puts up structures

explanation.surface: A building worker is beheaded when the government minister turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a clergyman in charge of a parish, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Criminal taking dope repeatedly at home

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word for dope appears twice

parts.note: dope is slang for a fool, an ass
in means at home

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker who keeps taking drugs at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs, but it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired killer is a criminal who murders to order.

clue.text: One is uplifted seeing such flags

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rises means goes up

explanation.surface: One is moved emotionally on seeing such banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' reads as banners; flag is also a name for the iris plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, so flags are these bulbous flowers.

clue.text: The know-all's sensible with port

parts.note: wise means sensible
Acre is a port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: The smart alec is sensible and drinks port.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to know everything, a smart alec.

clue.text: A number on horse-back get the bird

indicators.note: horse-back means the horse word is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
a net figure is a number after deductions

explanation.surface: A rider put on a horse's back gets the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' suggests being booed; 'get' is a link word and the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large white seabird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Top people can be bounders!

explanation.surface: Leaders can turn out to be cads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounders' looks like British slang for cads; read it literally as people who bound or jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Captains of ships or teams are top people, and those who hop and jump are bounders.
